output.brief:
What is going on: the stops are not mainly caused by the temps. Stops with a tagged person nearby stayed flat (about 41 to 44 a week), while stops with no tag nearby rose from about 164 to 607. Robots on firmware 6.4 in pallet zones A and B jumped from about 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 robot-hours, while the eight pallet robots still on 6.3 stayed flat at about 3.2. A bench test showed that 6.4 combined with the new glossy stretch film triggers stops on oblique pallet faces (17 of 20 passes), while 6.4 with the old matte film produced none. The likely driver is the firmware and new film interacting, not either alone. How sure I am: moderate. The bench test is one rig, and the 6.4.2 release is untested against this film.

What to do now: switch back to the matte film first, since it is reversible and the bench test supports it. Track stops by zone and firmware. Do not introduce the three-strike temp policy, and do not shorten the protective fields, since that weakens safety without fixing the cause. Do not wait on the December release. Check whether the 6.3 security waiver deadline of 31 October needs attention.
